description:
ATHERION Earth | Ember Trace

ATHERION Earth is a virtual team for NASA Space Apps 2026. We are tackling the MODIS and VIIRS Hot Spots challenge by developing a web application to explore satellite fire detections, historical patterns and sensor differences, with transparent data sources and uncertainty.

We welcome collaborators in Python, GIS, remote sensing, Earth science, web development, statistics and data visualization.

contacto : matiasjeremiasvillalba@gmail.com
summary:
EMBER TRACE, developed by ATHERION Earth, is a conceptual project addressing the challenge of harmonizing MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot observations.

Focused on Argentina, the project proposes a unified platform to explore historical thermal anomaly observations, compare satellite sensors, and understand spatial and temporal patterns of burning activity.

Its proposed features include an interactive map, historical filters, side-by-side sensor comparisons, statistical summaries, and transparent explanations of data limitations and methodology.

EMBER TRACE emphasizes that a satellite thermal anomaly does not necessarily confirm a wildfire. By promoting responsible interpretation and accessible comparison of NASA satellite resources, the project aims to support researchers, environmental analysts, and land managers.

The submission presents a conceptual solution and design proposal, not a fully implemented software application.
details:
EMBER TRACE is a conceptual platform designed to address the challenge of comparing MODIS and VIIRS active fire hotspot observations in a more accessible and transparent way.

The proposed workflow focuses on Argentina and includes an interactive map, historical and temporal filters, side-by-side satellite sensor comparisons, statistical summaries, and explanations of data sources, methodology, and limitations.

The project's main benefit is to help users explore historical thermal anomaly observations while understanding that satellite detections do not automatically represent confirmed wildfires. MODIS and VIIRS have different sensor characteristics, spatial resolutions, and observation times, which must be considered when interpreting their data.

The project is based on NASA FIRMS, NASA Earthdata, and VIIRS Fire Earth Science Data Record resources.

The team developed the project concept, documentation, and presentation materials. Canva was used for visual design, and ChatGPT assisted with brainstorming, writing, and organizing project documentation. GitHub Copilot was used for a commit-message suggestion.

No new software implementation or application code was developed during the hackathon. The interactive features described are proposed functionality, not operational features.

The project's creative approach combines scientific transparency, accessible data exploration, and responsible interpretation of satellite observations.
